from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines_text = [
            "RNNs process words sequentially, causing them to forget context.",
            "Long sentences lose critical connections between distant words.",
            "Human reading allows jumping between related ideas instantly."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Problem: Why Traditional Models Fail", lecture_lines_text)
        
        # Create RNN diagram elements (as per storyboard)
        rnn_nodes = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE) for _ in range(4)])
        rnn_nodes.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(rnn_nodes, 'C2')
        
        arrows = VGroup(*[Arrow(rnn_nodes[i].get_right(), rnn_nodes[i+1].get_left(), buff=0.1) for i in range(3)])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(rnn_nodes), Create(arrows))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        loss_arrow = CurvedArrow(rnn_nodes[0].get_top(), rnn_nodes[3].get_top(), color=RED, angle=-PI/3)
        self.play(Create(loss_arrow))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(rnn_nodes), FadeOut(arrows), FadeOut(loss_arrow))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Dot product measures how similar two words are.",
            "High dot product indicates strong contextual relevance.",
            "Softmax normalizes these scores into attention weights.",
            "Weights determine how much 'focus' to apply.",
            "Together, they map out relationships between all words."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Math: Dot Product and Softmax", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        dot_op = MathTex(r"\mathbf{Q} \cdot \mathbf{K}^T", color="#33FF57")
        softmax_curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.exp(x) / (1 + np.exp(x)), x_range=[-3, 3], color="#FF5733")
        attention_matrix = Matrix([[0.8, 0.2], [0.1, 0.9]], color="#3357FF").scale(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#33FF57"), Write(self.place_at_grid(dot_op, 'B3')))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.play(Indicate(dot_op))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF5733"), Create(self.place_at_grid(softmax_curve, 'D3')))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#3357FF"), FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(attention_matrix, 'B5')))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(FadeIn(attention_matrix))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "A single attention head limits contextual understanding.",
            "We use multiple heads to process information in parallel.",
            "Each head captures different linguistic features simultaneously.",
            "One head tracks grammar, another detects entities.",
            "Combining them builds a rich, deep understanding."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Multi-Head Attention: Seeing the Big Picture", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects for animations
        head1 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        head2 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5)
        head3 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(head1, "C2")
        self.play(Create(head1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.place_at_grid(head2, "C4")
        self.place_at_grid(head3, "C6")
        self.play(Create(head2), Create(head3))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(head1.animate.set_stroke(width=6), head2.animate.set_stroke(width=6), head3.animate.set_stroke(width=6))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        label1 = Text("Grammar", font_size=16).next_to(head1, DOWN)
        label2 = Text("Entities", font_size=16).next_to(head2, DOWN)
        self.add(label1, label2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        combined = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=PURPLE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(combined, "E4")
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(VGroup(head1, head2, head3), combined),
            FadeOut(label1, label2)
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read
outline.target_audience: University students with basic programming/math knowledge

sections.title: The Problem: Why Traditional Models Fail
sections.content: Introduce the limitation of RNNs (processing words linearly) which causes 'forgetting' at the end of long sentences. Contrast this with human reading, where we jump across sentences to connect related ideas.
sections.example: In the sentence: 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired,' humans instantly know 'it' refers to the 'animal'. Older models lose context after just a few words.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Query, Key, and Value
sections.content: Introduce the retrieval analogy. Query (what I'm looking for), Key (what I have to offer), and Value (the actual information). Use a visual search icon for Q, a label tag for K, and a document icon for V.
sections.example: Imagine a library: Your 'Query' is the search term, the book 'Key' is the title on the spine, and the 'Value' is the content inside the book.

sections.title: The Math: Dot Product and Softmax
sections.content: Explain how we calculate relevance: Dot product (Q·K^T) measures similarity (alignment). Softmax converts scores into percentages (attention weights). Visual: Heatmap matrix showing stronger connections as brighter colors.
sections.example: If Query is 'Animal' and Key is 'Tired', the dot product is high. If Query is 'Animal' and Key is 'Street', the dot product is low. Softmax ensures these weights sum to 100%.

sections.title: Multi-Head Attention: Seeing the Big Picture
sections.content: Explain that one 'head' isn't enough to understand complex language. We use multiple heads in parallel to focus on different aspects like grammar, sentiment, and entity relationships.
sections.example: Think of a team of analysts: Head 1 looks for grammar, Head 2 looks for the subject, Head 3 looks for emotional tone. Combining these gives a rich, multi-dimensional understanding.

sections.title: Summary and Application
sections.content: Recap how attention transforms raw text into a mathematical map of relationships, enabling LLMs to 'pay attention' to relevant words regardless of distance.
sections.example: When you ask ChatGPT to summarize a 50-page document, the Attention mechanism allows it to jump directly to the most relevant paragraphs while ignoring filler words.
